---
title: "Model and computation"
description: "Understand the driver, residual refresh rule and shared-kernel boundary."
---

## Composition and dependency direction

An S4 `fspec` contains two model components:

- `kernel`: an emhawkes `hspec`, without a residual law.
- `residual`: a `residual_law()` object.

Use `fkernel(model)` and `fresidual(model)` to read components, or the
corresponding replacement functions to update them. Replacement validates the
specification. Existing `$kernel` and `$residual` access remains supported.
The class also records the global refresh rule and a representation version;
it does not store evolving simulation state. The residual law remains S3.
Use `methods::is(model, "fspec")` for class checks; the new class does not
inherit the old S3 `frpp_spec` class.

The dependency is `frpp -> emhawkes`. The FRPP object does not inherit from
`hspec`, so Hawkes methods are not silently applied to it. The compatibility
adapter `as_legacy_hspec()` temporarily restores the older FRPP representation.


## Supply residual functions as needed

Use the same names as emhawkes: `dresidual` (density), `presidual` (CDF),
`qresidual` (quantile) and `rresidual` (generator). All default to NULL.
The constructor needs at least a density or generator; each operation then
checks only its own requirements before evaluating callbacks or drawing randomness.

| Operation | Required residual functions |
|---|---|
| Simulation | rresidual |
| Univariate likelihood and fitting | dresidual |
| Multivariate likelihood and fitting | dresidual, presidual |
| Residual diagnostics with infer = TRUE | dresidual, presidual, qresidual |

For simulation alone:

```{r residual-generator-only}
simulation_law <- frpp::residual_law(c(rate = 1), rresidual = stats::rexp)
simulation_model <- frpp::fspec(
  methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1), simulation_law)
simulation_path <- frpp::fsim(simulation_model, size = 5, seed = 73,
  lambda_component0 = 0)
simulation_path$inter_arrival
```

The aliases `density`, `cdf`, `quantile` and `rng` remain supported without
warnings, in that order. You can mix names for different roles, but supplying
both non-NULL names for one role is an error. The original six positional
arguments retain their order. Saved laws retain their existing internal
representation and callback environments/defaults; no conversion is needed.

## Exponential state and event mapping

For event type \(i\), the numeric driver is
\[
v_i(t) = \mu_i + \sum_{j=1}^K C_{ij}(t).
\]
Between events, each component decays exponentially. In the currently supported
FRPP simulation interface, the decay rates are equal within each row.

An event's type identifies a **row** of the driver. Its `type_col_map` entry
selects the **columns** updated after the event. Entries can contain several
columns and can overlap across event types. With numeric marked effects, a
selected component receives
\[
\alpha_{ij} + \eta_{ij}(m-1).
\]
Rows are event types; columns are kernels. They need not have the same count.

The state layer can represent signed components without clipping them.
Simulation still requires a valid nonnegative driver and arrival calculation;
a valid component shape alone does not establish simulation support.

## The residual refresh rule

After every event in the combined process, the simulator draws a candidate
residual for every dimension, inverts each integrated driver and selects the
earliest event. All candidates are refreshed at the next global event.

This is **not** a model where a dimension keeps its own residual clock until
that dimension fires. Carrying candidates across other dimensions' events
would change the model for a general residual law.

For an inter-event interval, let
\[
A_i = \int v_i(t)\,dt.
\]
If type \(j\) fires, the log-likelihood contribution is
\[
\log v_j + \log f(A_j) + \sum_{i\ne j}\log S(A_i),
\]
where \(f\) and \(S\) are the residual density and survival function.
Unit-exponential residuals reduce this expression to a Hawkes contribution.

For other laws, the driver is not automatically the conditional intensity:
the residual hazard also matters. The current observation API ends at the
last recorded event; it does not add a separate terminal observation interval.

## Computation backends

| Operation | Current implementation |
|---|---|
| Default simulation, `bridge` | Uses the existing public emhawkes FRPP event loop |
| Optional simulation, `state` | FRPP owns the event loop, using public event-wise kernel calculations |
| Default likelihood, `bridge` | Uses emhawkes's existing FRPP likelihood |
| Experimental likelihood, `state` | Uses public kernel replay, then assembles FRPP density and survival contributions |
| Default estimation, `fit_backend = "bridge"` | `ffit()` supplies an FRPP objective to public emhawkes fitting |
| Optional independent estimation | FRPP prepares observations, registers parameters through the public plan, runs maxLik or stats directly and reconstructs its model |

The `state` backend requires numeric baseline and kernel parameters, equal
decay rates within a row, and no impact or mark-density callbacks. Numeric
`eta`, observed marks and kernel mappings are supported. It requires the
public shared-kernel API available in GitHub development emhawkes 1.0.1.9000
and reports an explicit error when that API is absent. The
[shared-kernel guide](https://ksublee.github.io/emhawkes/articles/shared-kernel.html)
defines its input and output contract.

Replay supplies kernel-only interval integrals, pre-event sums and a final
component state. FRPP adds the baseline contribution. Full component histories
are requested only for `infer = TRUE`; interval integrals and sums still require
storage proportional to observations times event types.

The default `bridge` remains available for callback models. The existing
`emhawkes.engine` option retains its Hawkes likelihood meaning; it does not
select a native FRPP likelihood.

## Initialization and inference boundaries

FRPP automatic initialization uses zero components and recommends an explicit
state. A Hawkes unconditional mean is not assumed for arbitrary residual laws.

The shared state calculation does not establish stationarity, identification
or confidence-interval coverage. FRPP fitting uses its own likelihood and
optimizer curvature; Hawkes-specific Hessian stabilization is not applied.

The old `frpp_spec()` constructor and serialized class remain compatible.
`as_fspec()` converts an older FRPP `hspec` or either saved S3 specification
class to S4. Public operations also accept those S3 specifications. Callback functions keep their
environments and default bindings during conversion.

## Migration from emhawkes

FRPP-specific functionality is planned to move to frpp. The
[FRPP examples](frpp-examples.html) use the new interface; the
[legacy vignette](emhawkes-compatibility.html) preserves the full original
emhawkes examples, including fitting and reconstruction.

Simple custom-residual models remain available in emhawkes during the transition.
No existing residual-law function or slot is removed by this documentation move.
Hawkes goodness-of-fit residual diagnostics remain in emhawkes.

## Next development steps

The numeric independent FRPP simulator is available as an optional backend.
Callback simulation and independent estimation reconstruction remain future work.
The current public replay API is a first shared calculation boundary, not a
complete separation of the two packages' engines.


## Independent numeric simulation

```{r independent-simulation, eval=FALSE}
path <- fsim(model, size = 1000, seed = 73, lambda_component0 = 0,
             backend = "state")
```

This requires the event-wise APIs in current GitHub development emhawkes.
FRPP draws one residual vector for all dimensions, inverts its integrated drivers
with a prepared `exp_kernel_plan()` when available, chooses the first minimum
by row, and calls its `step()` function to decay and update mapped columns. It records the original
path fields, counts and component histories. No hsim call or growing-prefix
replay occurs in this backend. The plan validates fixed kernel parameters and
baseline once; changing components and residual targets remain checked. It stores
no current state. Installations with the earlier event-wise API use its checked
`exp_kernel_wait()` and `exp_kernel_step()` calls instead. The shared calculation
layer contains no RNG.

The first scope is plain numeric baseline and kernel parameters, including
numeric eta, zero baselines and admissible signed components. No baseline,
impact, mark-generator or mark-density event callbacks run in this backend.
Marks are one. Residual generators are retained with their existing parameter
binding and run once per attempted global event. Current-state validity is
checked before each new draw, and an error never restarts the bridge.

`bridge` remains the default because the reference independent loop is slower
for large paths. `backend = "auto"` is an explicit opt-in selector: it uses
state when the model and installed APIs support it, otherwise bridge. Forced
state reports unsupported models before drawing. Simulation selection is
independent of the likelihood backend and `emhawkes.engine`.

See the repository's [simulation validation report](https://github.com/ksublee/frpp/blob/main/tools/independent-simulation-results.md)
for exact-result, RNG, timing and allocation checks. Reported allocations are
cumulative Rprofmem records, not peak resident memory.


## Parameter registration and fitted-model reconstruction

For numeric kernels without event callbacks and raw residual laws,
`ffit()` registers kernel matrices and the residual parameter vector through
the public emhawkes `parameter_plan()` contract. Numeric matrix coordinates
retain their existing reduced/full sharing rules; named residual coordinates
retain their names. Fixed residual laws stay outside the fitted coordinate set.

Optimization still uses public `hfit()` with the FRPP objective. The same
parameter map rules, fixed selectors, constraints and optimizer controls apply.
After optimization, frpp restores numeric components and assembles its own
kernel/residual model through the public plan. Callback/bound-law models and
older emhawkes versions retain the existing fitted_hspec reconstruction.

The raw optimizer result and saved ffit representation remain available.
This step separates registration/restoration; optimizer adapters and legacy
objective preparation remain shared. It makes no new confidence-interval
coverage or performance claim.


## Independent numeric fitting

`fit_backend` selects who runs estimation; `backend` selects the likelihood.
Both defaults remain `"bridge"`. For example:

```{r}
model <- frpp::fspec(methods::new("hspec", mu = 1, alpha = 0, beta = 1),
  frpp::residual_law(c(rate = 1), dresidual = stats::dexp))
fit <- frpp::ffit(model, c(0, .2, .3, .5), optimizer = "stats",
  fixed = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), lambda_component0 = 0,
  fit_backend = "independent")
stats::coef(fit)
fit$fitting
```

This path supports plain numeric mu/alpha/beta/eta, kernel mappings and raw
residual laws. It owns observation/count validation, explicit initial states,
optimizer calls and result assembly. The public parameter plan retains matrix
sharing, coordinate order and named residual sharing. Fixed/free selectors,
linear constraints, box bounds, optional derivatives and validator rejection
follow the existing provider rules. It uses no emhawkes internal functions and
does not call hfit. The selected likelihood may still use the public bridge.

Callback kernels, event callbacks, legacy bound residual laws and dependencies
without the parameter API retain bridge fitting. An explicit independent request
reports unsupported cases; `fit_backend = "auto"` records its selected route and
fallback reason before optimization. A failed optimization is never retried on
another path. New results retain the existing ffit accessors. The raw independent
stats provider result has its own frpp_stats_fit class; maxLik retains its class.
The saved result's fitting field reports the route, while numerical diagnostics
retain their existing meaning. Unavailable Wald covariance remains unavailable.
